title: Freight Forwarding Manager (Sea & Air)
description: How would you like to build and lead the freight forwarding division of a logistics tech startup based in Ethiopia, starting with sea freight? How would you feel about being part of a Team that is on a mission to fix an incredibly inefficient logistics industry? (Apply Here: https://jobs.worksimplehr.com/jobs/garri-logistics-plc-1/logistics-manager-freight-forwarding-sea-air) What's The Job? As Freight Forwarding Manager, your task is to set up and run Garri's freight forwarding business from the ground up, with sea freight at its core: Build the division: services, processes, SOPs, pricing, and the team. Own sea freight imports and exports end to end (FCL, LCL, break bulk, RoRo, and project cargo): vessel booking, documentation, Djibouti port handling, transit, customs clearance, and final delivery. Run the Djibouti side of the operation: vessel arrivals, port and transit agents, free time, and getting cargo out of port fast. Choose the right import mode (multimodal or unimodal) for each shipment, and coordinate with Modjo and other dry ports. Build and manage relationships with shipping lines, NVOCCs, overseas agents, Djibouti transit agents, and clearing agents. Negotiate ocean freight rates and contracts, prepare competitive quotations, and protect the margin on every shipment. Grow air freight as a second service line, working with airlines and air cargo agents. Lead the licensing and regulatory setup for freight forwarding and customs clearance, and keep the division fully compliant. Win and grow customers (importers, exporters, manufacturers, and project cargo clients), including client meetings and tenders. Connect forwarding with Garri's trucking network and technology to offer true door-to-door service. Control costs and risks: demurrage, detention, storage, cargo insurance, claims, and the cash flow tied to freight and duties. Report volumes, revenue, margins, transit times, and customer satisfaction to management every month. Recruit, train, and lead the team, starting with an Ocean Freight Officer, and set clear targets for each person. Perform other duties assigned by the General Manager. Who Are We? Garri Logistics is a digital freight brokerage and fleet management platform in Ethiopia. We are building innovative tech products and services to bring a highly fragmented, low trust, and offline freight industry to an online marketplace while bringing much needed trust, quality, cost saving, and efficiency. Our goal is to make Garri Logistics the primary way to transport goods across Ethiopia. We are now adding sea and air freight forwarding, so our customers can move their cargo with one trusted partner, from the port of origin all the way to their door. What Skills Do You Need? 8+ years' experience in freight forwarding, including at least 5 years in sea freight operations and 3 years in a management role. Deep, hands-on sea freight expertise: FCL, LCL, break bulk, and project cargo, carrier bookings, bills of lading, and container management (free time, demurrage, detention). Strong knowledge of the Djibouti corridor, multimodal and unimodal imports, Ethiopian customs procedures, eSW, and dry port operations. Existing relationships with shipping lines, NVOCCs, overseas agents, Djibouti transit agents, and clearing agents. Solid understanding of Incoterms, letters of credit and bank documents, and cargo insurance. Proven record of winning customers and running a profitable forwarding operation or branch. Experience setting up a new division or office is a strong plus. Air freight experience (airline bookings, air waybills) is a plus. Comfortable with technology, and excited to help shape the software behind our forwarding business. Excellent leadership, organization, and entrepreneurial spirit (work under little or no guidance, and perform under pressure). Bachelor's degree in Logistics, Supply Chain Management, Maritime Studies, Business, or a related field. Excellent written and verbal English and Amharic skills. Compensation We offer competitive salary and benefits, and amazing opportunities to grow with us. What's In It For You? If you are looking for a rare chance to build a freight forwarding business from the ground up, backed by an established trucking network and our own technology, then this is a good fit. We are actively interviewing and looking to onboard quickly.

title: JPO - Strategic Planning and Analysis Analyst
description: Job Description IMPORTANT : This position is offered within the framework of the Junior Professional Officer (JPO) Programme and is open exclusively to nationals of Norway . Applicants must meet the eligibility requirements established for the JPO Programme and the specific requirements of the position. The UNDP Junior Professional Officer (JPO) Programme The UNDP (United Nations Development Programme) JPO Programme equips outstanding young leaders with the skills and experience required to advance the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) and make a positive difference in the world. As a pathway into the world of development, the programme offers young professionals excellent exposure to multilateral cooperation and sustainable development while providing a valuable entry point into the UN system. During their assignments, JPOs benefit from the guidance of experienced UNDP staff members and are actively involved in supporting the design and implementation of UNDP’s programs within UNDP’s headquarters, regional or country offices. Additionally, the JPO will undergo a journey of exposure and growth which will build both personal and professional capacity for a career within the multilateral development sector. As a JPO and young professional in UNDP you should be interested in pursuing a global career with aspiration to work for a field-based organization in support of the development agenda. The JPO will work as part of a team and be supervised by an experienced UNDP staff member, including : Structured guidance and feedback, especially in the beginning of the assignment, with the purpose of gradually increasing of responsibilities Establishment of a work plan, with clear key results Guidance and advice in relation to learning and training opportunities within the field of expertise Completion of the yearly UNDP Annual Performance Review (APR) including learning and development objectives. The JPO will benefit from the following learning and development opportunities: Participation in a virtual Programme Policy and Operations Induction Course within the first 4 to 6 months of assignment Use of yearly JPO duty-related travel and training allocation (DTTA), as per the online DTTA guide On-going Masterclasses on relevant and inspiring themes Career development support mechanisms and activities Networking with fellow JPOs, young professionals and senior UNDP colleagues Mentoring programme Other training and learning opportunities Organisational context The United Nations Development Programme (UNDP) is supporting the Government of Ethiopia in the implementation of the National Disarmament, Demobilization, and Reintegration Programme (NDRP) as part of broader efforts to consolidate peace and support recovery in conflict-affected regions. The NDRP is being implemented in diverse and politically sensitive settings, including Tigray, Oromia, Amhara, and other areas affected by conflict. These regions vary significantly in terms of their political dynamics, levels of insecurity, and the socio-economic realities faced by ex-combatants and host communities. In this context, the need for clear, consistent, and conflict-sensitive communication is paramount. The dissemination of DDR objectives and progress must be tailored to regional specificities while ensuring alignment with national narratives. Misinformation, political contestation, and diverging public expectations pose significant risks to the credibility and perceived neutrality of the DDR programme. As such, strategic communication and risk analysis are critical to mitigating tensions, building trust, and maintaining the programme’s momentum. This position is therefore essential to ensure UNDP’s work remains responsive to local realities, politically informed, and strategically positioned in Ethiopia’s complex recovery and peacebuilding landscape. UNDP’s DDR Unit in Ethiopia supports the nationally led stabilization and recovery process by coordinating development partner engagement and managing pooled funding in support of the National Demobilization and Reintegration Programme (NDRP), which is implemented by the National Rehabilitation Commission (NRC). The Unit’s key priorities include ensuring coherence among donor-supported initiatives, promoting conflict-sensitive programming, facilitating regional and federal-level coordination, and supporting monitoring, learning, and accountability frameworks. Given the diverse operational settings in which the NDRP is being implemented—including regions with different political dynamics, conflict legacies, and levels of community acceptance—the work of the DDR Unit is shaped by the need for careful messaging, timely political analysis, and strong collaboration with implementing and funding partners. This position is thus integral to ensuring that risk-informed, adaptive, and context-sensitive communication supports national DDR efforts and contributes to broader peacebuilding and stabilization outcomes. title: 23257 Chief Migration Health Officer (P)
description:
Under the direct supervision of the Chief of Mission (COM), and the technical supervision of the Regional Health Assessment Programme Coordinator (RHAPC) and in coordination with the Head of Programmes and the Regional Migration Health Specialist for your region, the Chief Migration Health Officer will be responsible for the development, implementation, and management of the Health Assessment and other health programmes. Responsibilities and Accountabilities Health Assessment Portfolio Organize and supervise the migration health assessment process to fulfil the technical requirements of the resettlement countries in the areas of: 1. Medical examinations 2. Imaging 3. Laboratory testing 4. Vaccinations 5. TB management 6. Treatment and referrals 7. Pre-departure procedures and medical movements 8. Documentation, certification and information transmission 9. Other technical areas as may be required Ensure that the infrastructure and equipment of Health Assessment Programme (HAP) premises meet professional standards of quality and safety and are sufficient and adequate for the provision of the services. Ensure that human resources and HAP organizational structure are sufficient and adequate for the planned levels of health assessments and that the staff have the necessary qualifications and skills. Establish a sufficient network of external human resources, such as consultants and medical escorts, to support the health assessment process and travel assistance. In coordination with the Human Resource Unit, ensure that all medical personnel maintain valid licenses to practice. Ensure that the regulatory government authorities are informed about IOM’s health activities and that the IOM medical facilities have obtained approval to provide health assessments and related services. Establish and maintain efficient, client-centered procedures and ensure a high level of integrity at all stages of the HAP process, including client information and appointment system, payment, registration, pre- and post-test counselling, examination, testing, treatment and referrals, submission of health assessment results, pre-departure and other procedures. Establish and maintain a system enabling clients to provide feedback. Establish and maintain a system of quality improvement for each service area. Undertake quality control activities on a regular basis; practice observation and regular supervisory visits to all facilities/teams involved in the health assessment operations. desk audits and use self-assessment tools. Use data analysis and a web reporting system to monitor performance indicators. Ensure implementation of the global IOM Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs); create and implement country-specific SOPs for each service area. Ensure proper reporting and management of incidents according to the Guidance Note for Incident Management. Incorporate additional public health interventions in the HAP context. Such interventions may include surveillance for communicable diseases, outbreak preparedness and response, health education and health promotion, public health services for host communities, liaison with public health institutions, and other activities. Supervise health and non-health staff as well as external consultants involved in the health assessment process; ensure that performance evaluations for health staff are completed in a timely manner. Ensure that all staff are aware of the IOM Standards of Conduct under Article 42, and continuously reinforce these standards. Inform in due time the COM and the IOM Ethics Committee of any issues regarding staff misconduct. Establish the HAP staff development strategy and ensure that the appropriate plan is implemented. Within that plan, apart from attendance at external educational events, initiate, organize, and deliver various professional in-house trainings. Liaise with external service providers to negotiate agreements in coordination with the Resource Management Officer (RMO). To the extent possible, exercise quality control over outsourced services and take corrective measures if necessary. Liaise with relevant partners at government level, immigration and health authorities of the receiving countries, as well as other international UN and non-UN agencies, Non-Governmental Organizations (NGOs), donor community and national partners. Maintain confidentiality and security of migration health data in accordance with the IOM Data Protection Principles. Organize systematic collection, processing, and analyses of migration health data. Ensure data quality. Provide periodic, as well as ad hoc reporting to the Migration Health Division (MHD) for Migration Health (MH) activities. Oversee the financial aspects of the health programmes in close coordination with the mission's finance staff: supervise budget preparation and ensure monitoring of MH projects, suggest adjustments and cost-effective solutions, and review financial reports. Provide oversight and coordinate procurement of medical equipment, vaccines, medications, and other medical supplies in coordination with the resource management unit. Organize and supervise activities of mobile medical teams, if applicable. Other Health Activities In coordination with the Head of Office (HOO)/COM, reinforce partnerships and liaise with the Migration Health (MH) sector with the Ministry of Health, health institutions and academia, as well as other relevant leading agencies. Incorporate multi-sectoral approaches to partnerships, as well as capitalize on IOM strengths across all service areas within the overall framework of IOM’s 12-point Strategy adopted by IOM Member States (June 2007). Conceptualize, develop and implement appropriate migration health-related projects that may benefit migrants, Internally Displaced Persons (IDPs) and host communities as well as conflict/natural disaster affected population in coordination with relevant Units, the Regional Thematic Specialists (RTSs) and other colleagues. Facilitate the integration of health assessment activities into the overall migration-related programming of the Country Office through close collaboration with the various units at the Country Office level. Advise IOM colleagues on the link between the Health Assessment Programme with the two other core MHD programme areas - Health Promotion and Assistance to Migrants, and Migration Health Assistance to Crisis-Affected Populations. Identify opportunities for expanding migration health activities and programmes by informing embassies and consulates of IOM’s migration health work and lobbying for IOM Migration Health Assessment Centres (MHACs) becoming panel sites for Migration Health Assessments (MHA), responding to announcements for calls for proposals by drafting project concept notes and/or proposals and liaising with UN agencies and the Ministry of Health to identify project development opportunities. Perform such other duties as may be assigned. Required Qualifications and Experience Education University degree in Medicine from an accredited academic institution with preferred specializations: internal medicine and its subspecialties, Paediatrics, Anaesthesiology, Emergency Medicine, Family Medicine, Obstetrics and Gynaecology; and a minimum of nine years of relevant professional experience, of which at least three years of managerial responsibilities; or, University degree in Medicine from an accredited academic institution with preferred specializations: internal medicine and its subspecialties, Paediatrics, Anaesthesiology, Emergency Medicine, Family Medicine, Obstetrics and Gynaecology, plus Master’s Degree in Community or Public Health, Medical Specialization in Infectious Diseases, Tropical Medicine, or other related fields from an accredited academic institution, with seven years of relevant professional experience, of which at least three years of managerial responsibilities. Accredited Universities are those listed in the UNESCO World Higher Education Database. Experience Professional continuous clinical experience, preferably in a multidisciplinary hospital setting or at IOM/similar international clinic context; Experience in Migration Health Assessments; Demonstrated progressive experience in health programme management; Experience in project development, management, and report writing; and, Experience in migration health emergency response is an asset. Skills Effective managerial and leadership skills; Proven abilities to establish partnerships with government institutions, health institutions, and other partners; Knowledge of public health; Demonstrable knowledge of patient safety and infection prevention and control; Organizational skills; and, Communication skills. Languages For this position, fluency in English is required (oral and written). Working knowledge of another official UN languages (Arabic, Chinese, French, Russian, and Spanish) is an advantage. Through partnership and collaborations, we work to ensure the inclusion of older people across society and strive to deliver a just and fair world for everyone as they get older. Our work is driven by our desire to achieve real impact for older people, to be inclusive, to work in partnership and to learn from our shared experience. About the Job The MEAL Officer plays a critical role in enhancing the quality, effectiveness, and accountability of HelpAge’s global programmes, advocacy efforts, and organizational performance. This role coordinates and provides technical input into the design and implementation of monitoring and evaluation (M&E) frameworks, supports learning processes, and provides technical advice to teams and Network Members. The postholder will work collaboratively across teams and Impact Vehicles to coordinates performance measurement, evaluations, rapid needs assessments and key planning and reporting processes, ensuring that HelpAge’s programmes and influencing initiatives are grounded in evidence, informed by the voices of older people, and contribute to a strong culture of learning, transparency, and continuous improvement. Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities 1. Organisational Performance and Monitoring and Evaluation Frameworks Coordinate and provide technical input into the development and implementation of robust M&E frameworks and tools for global programmes, advocacy initiatives, and Impact Vehicles. Support Impact Vehicle, cross-functional, and programmes teams in defining indicators, setting baselines, and tracking outcomes aligned to HelpAge’s Global Impact Framework. Coordinate the development and review of results frameworks, log frames, indicators, baselines, and targets across teams and Impact Vehicles. Lead the identification and development of appropriate data sources, data-collection methodologies and evidence requirements for organisational and Impact Vehicle indicators and targets. Act as the organisational focal point for standardising KPI measurement across all Impact Vehicles, establishing and maintaining consistent indicator definitions, measurement tools, evidence requirements and reporting approaches, subject to final technical sign-off by the Global Impact Adviser. Coordinate organisation-wide Impact Vehicle performance tracking, working with relevant teams to ensure the timely and consistent collection, analysis and reporting of results. Coordinate and undertake the drafting and revision of organisational MEAL policies, procedures, standards and guidance. 2. Technical MEL Support for Global Impact Team Provide advanced technical MEAL advice, support, and quality assurance across HelpAge’s global programme portfolio, working with programme teams and Network Members throughout proposal development, programme design, implementation, monitoring, reporting and learning. Provide technical support to advocacy teams to track and measure the outcomes and influence of campaigns, policy engagement, and strategic partnerships. Develop and apply methodologies and tools for monitoring policy change, stakeholder influence, and advocacy impact. 3. Accountability and Participation Provide guidance on participatory monitoring approaches, ensuring meaningful inclusion of older people and marginalised groups. Work with programme and network member teams to build inclusive, culturally appropriate feedback and response systems at community or country level. Collaborate with the Data and Accountability Officer to ensure feedback data is analysed and used to inform adaptive programming and advocacy refinement. Promote transparency, responsiveness, and power-sharing through strengthened accountability practices. 4. Organisational Learning and Knowledge Sharing Coordinate learning reviews, after-action reviews, and annual and mid-term reflection processes within and across teams. Document and disseminate key learning, good practices, and innovations. Facilitate cross-organisational learning events, webinars, and communities of practice. 5. Rapid Needs Assessments Act as HelpAge’s technical focal point for rapid needs assessments, establishing and maintaining organisational methodologies, tools, standards and guidance.Advise and coordinate teams undertaking rapid needs assessments, determining appropriate sampling approaches, data-collection methods, questionnaire design, analytical process, and quality-assurance requirements Undertake the coordination and final technical quality assurance of rapid needs assessment reports, including establishing requirements and timelines, coordinating and consolidating inputs from colleagues, and ensuring that findings and recommendations are methodologically robust, supported by the available evidence and suitable for organisational or external use. 6. Support the development of evaluation terms of reference and methodologies, and support the process, from inception, data collection, analysis and delivery. Capacity Strengthening Design and deliver training and tailored support to HelpAge teams, partners, and network members on MEL and accountability. Develop user-friendly guidance, templates, and toolkits to strengthen MEL practices across the organisation. Build internal capacity for adaptive management and evidence use in decision-making. 7. Desirable Excellent communication skills in English (spoken and written); Fluency in one or more additional languages used in the Global South (e.g., Spanish, French, Arabic) are highly desirable. Department: Network Development Team, Global Impact Directorate Reports to (Line Manager): Regional Adviser, Africa Responsible for( Line managing): N/A Grade: C Contract Type: Fixed-term, 18 months, with scope to extend subject to funding About HelpAge HelpAge International works with a diverse global network of around 200 organisations across 99 countries to promote the rights of older people to lead dignified, healthy and secure lives. Through partnership and collaborations, we work to ensure the inclusion of older people across society and strive to deliver a just and fair world for everyone as they get older. Our work is driven by our desire to achieve real impact for older people, to be inclusive, to work in partnership and to learn from our shared experience. About the Job The Africa conference & Regional PlatformCoordinator role provides dedicated coordination capacity for the co-creation and delivery of the Africa Ageing Conference and agreed coordination and implementation support to the Africa Coordination Mechanism as a regional platform. The postholder will translate strategic direction and partner decisions into clear plans, well-managed processes, effective meetings and timely follow-through. It will connect conference delivery with year-round regional platform coordination, ensuring that network member priorities, evidence and learning inform continental dialogue and action, and that commitments arising from convenings are captured and progressed. Purpose of the role To lead the day-to-day coordination of the Africa Ageing Conference and provide coordination and implementation support to the operation and development of the Africa Coordination Mechanism, under the leadership of the Regional Advisor, Africa. The postholder will bring structure to complex multi-stakeholder processes, maintain high-quality information and partner-management systems, coordinate events and working groups, and ensure decisions, dependencies, risks and commitments are actively managed and followed through. Additionally, the postholder will work closely with the Africa Resource Mobilisation & Partnerships Manager , ensuring that Conference plans, priorities and resource requirements inform fundraising, sponsorship and partner engagement. Key areas for impact/influence and responsibilities 1. Africa Ageing Conference co-coordination and delivery Lead the day-to-day coordination and delivery of the Africa Ageing Conference, working with the Regional Advisor, Africa, the Conference Planning and Coordination Team, network members and partners. Coordinate implementation of the Conference workplan, milestones, dependencies and delivery schedule. Support Conference governance and working arrangements, including planning groups and technical workstreams. Monitor progress, risks, issues and resource requirements, escalating and supporting resolution as required. Coordinate partner engagement, Conference meetings and consultations, ensuring effective preparation, documentation and follow-up. Support post-Conference follow-up, accountability and implementation of agreed commitments and actions. 2. Africa Coordination Mechanism and sub-regional platform coordination Support the operation and development of the Africa Coordination Mechanism as a platform for collective leadership, collaboration and action. Coordinate meetings, consultations, learning exchanges and working sessions linked to the Mechanism. Support engagement by network members, national and sub-regional platforms, older people's organisations and strategic regional partners. Coordinate follow-up on agreed priorities, decisions and commitments, ensuring clear ownership and accountability. Facilitate connections between Network priorities, regional platforms, Conference planning and wider influencing opportunities. 3. Knowledge management, reporting and partner follow-up Maintain systems for tracking key decisions, actions, commitments, learning and implementation progress arising from the Conference and Africa Coordination Mechanism. Coordinate regular reporting on progress against agreed priorities, milestones and commitments. Capture and synthesise emerging learning, good practice and recommendations to inform future planning and collective action. Support development of reports, briefings, knowledge products and partner communications relating to implementation of the Africa Plan. Skills and experience required Essential Degree in International Development, Public Policy, International Relations, Social Sciences, Public Administration, Event or Conference Management, or a related field, or equivalent professional experience. Substantial experience coordinating complex regional, multi-country or multi-stakeholder programmes, networks, partnerships or convenings with demonstrated responsibility for translating plans and decisions into delivery. Demonstrable experience coordinating the planning and delivery of regional or international conferences, major events, policy forums or multi-stakeholder initiatives. Strong project coordination skills, including workplanning, action tracking, meeting coordination, stakeholder follow-up and risk or issue escalation. Experience working with civil society networks, membership organisations, regional platforms or multi-partner coalitions. Excellent written communication skills, including preparation of agendas, minutes, briefings, reports, trackers and concise partner-facing materials. Excellent information-management skills, with strong attention to detail and the ability to maintain accurate records across multiple workstreams. Confidence coordinating senior stakeholders and partners across institutions, countries and cultures. Ability to coordinate multiple workstreams simultaneously and work effectively across time zones. Fluency in English. Desirable Knowledge of African Union, Regional Economic Community or UN coordination structures. Experience working with African regional institutions, government stakeholders, UN agencies, development partners or international organisations. Knowledge of ageing, demographic change, health and care, social protection, human rights, gender, climate resilience, humanitarian action or inclusive development. Experience coordinating technical working groups, regional platforms, conference programmes, partner roundtables or high-level event logistics. Experience supporting sponsorship or donor-engagement processes in collaboration with fundraising colleagues. French, Portuguese or Arabic language skills. Key Behavioural Competencies Working Collaboratively with Others: Work collaboratively, building mutual trust and respect, with external organizations and partners to achieve our strategic aims and objectives; being accountable for the work we do together. Adaptability and Flexibility: Adapt to new directions or opportunities arising within the organisation and in our work area; being flexible in our role, constantly using the feedback to learn more and evolve further. Supporting and Facilitating Change: Lead behavioural and cultural change through embracing a supportive, collaborative and highly inclusive environment where everybody feels supported, respected and engaged. Extend HelpAge’s Reach and Impact: Extend HelpAge’s reach and impact by creating and identifying new business development opportunities and building relationships with new partners. Diversity and Inclusion: Lead and promote a culture of including the voices of older people across our support, convening and thought leadership roles, in a way that is transformative, empowering and highly inclusive of those marginalised by gender, economic status, disability and other factors of discrimination. Leading Others (for managers): Demonstrate strong leadership to own unit/department and manage people in a well and reputable manner. Create an atmosphere of trust and an enabling environment where staff can contribute their best and develop their potential. Policies and Code of Conduct As a HelpAge International employee, you are expected to comply with all organisational policies and standards, and to conduct yourself in a manner consistent with our values at all times. This includes, but is not limited to: Code of Conduct Safeguarding Policy and Prevention of Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (PSEA) Anti-Fraud and Bribery Policy Anti-Bullying, Harassment and Sexual Harassment Policy Diversity, Equity and Inclusion Policy Raising a Concern (Whistleblowing) Policy Social Media Policy All staff are required to familiarise themselves with these policies, complete any mandatory training, and adhere to them throughout their employment with HelpAge International Safeguarding HelpAge International is committed to safeguarding the communities with which we work, our partners, staff and any others who we come into contact with. The post holder will also be responsible for: Preventing harm and abuse from our people, operations and programmes to anyone that encounters our work. Reporting all safeguarding incidents you see, hear, hear about or suspect, using our internal reporting mechanism. Complying with all safeguarding framework policies and practices. Completing mandatory training courses relating to our safeguarding policy framework and complying with HR vetting procedures.

title: Regional Finance Controller - Kenya
description:
Location: Nairobi, Kenya (for exceptional candidates, we are open to other countries where IRW has a country office in the African region) Contract: Permanent Salary: £38,322 Closing Date: 11th October 2026 Islamic Relief Worldwide (IRW) is a faith-based humanitarian and development organisation working to save and transform the lives of some of the world's most vulnerable people. Established in 1984 and operating in over 45 countries, we respond to emergencies, tackle poverty, empower communities, and advocate for lasting change. We are seeking an experienced and strategic Regional Finance Controller - Africa (West and East) to join our Finance & Corporate Services Division. This is a unique opportunity for a senior finance leader who is passionate about financial governance, capacity building, compliance, and driving sustainable improvement across complex international operations. The preferred location for this role is Nairobi, Kenya. However, we recognise that exceptional talent exists across the continent and will consider applications from suitably qualified candidates located within Africa who can support the regional travel requirements and responsibilities of the position. The Finance & Corporate Services Division is a strategic enabler of organisational performance, accountability and sustainability, delivering integrated services across Finance, Treasury, ERP & Digital Transformation, ICT, Supply Chain and Facilities. As part of an ambitious finance transformation programme, the division is strengthening financial governance, independent oversight, service excellence, and data-driven decision making across the organisation's global footprint. About the Role The Regional Finance Controller (RFC) is responsible for providing financial oversight, governance, assurance, compliance, and capacity building across Islamic Relief's country offices and implementing partners throughout West and East Africa. This is far more than a traditional financial control role. You will work closely with Country Directors, Finance Managers, operational teams, and local partners to strengthen financial management practices, build organisational capability, and ensure the highest standards of financial stewardship are embedded across the region. You will play a critical leadership role in improving financial performance, enhancing internal control frameworks, strengthening donor and statutory compliance, and supporting long-term financial sustainability. Through visible, hands-on engagement with country offices and partners, you will help drive a step-change in financial discipline, transparency, accountability, and decision-making. The role combines strategic oversight with practical delivery. You will be responsible for assessing financial performance, mentoring regional finance teams, identifying and mitigating risk, supporting fraud prevention initiatives, and ensuring finance effectively supports programme delivery and donor confidence. Reporting to the Global Finance Operations Lead, you will provide expert technical guidance and leadership across a diverse and complex regional portfolio, supporting the ongoing evolution of Islamic Relief's global finance operating model. The successful candidate will spend approximately 50% of their time travelling across the region, providing direct support to country offices, finance teams, and implementing partners. The Successful Candidate Will Have: A professionally recognised accounting qualification (ACCA, CIMA, ICAEW, ICMA or equivalent). Significant senior-level financial management experience, ideally within the humanitarian, NGO, development, or international non-profit sector. Demonstrable experience leading financial governance, compliance, assurance, and internal control activities across multiple entities or geographical locations. Strong expertise in budgeting, forecasting, financial modelling, financial planning, and scenario analysis. Experience producing consolidated management accounts, variance analysis, financial performance reporting, and strategic financial insight. Proven experience managing donor compliance requirements and statutory obligations. A strong understanding of financial risk management, fraud prevention, and control frameworks. Experience leading, developing, mentoring, and coaching finance teams. Excellent stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence and support both finance and non-finance leaders. Strong communication skills and the ability to present complex financial information clearly and effectively. Experience designing and delivering finance training, capability building, and development programmes. High levels of integrity, accountability, professionalism, and cultural sensitivity. Commitment to the mission, vision, and values of Islamic Relief Worldwide. Fluency in both English and French. Desirable Experience managing donor-funded programmes and institutional grant reporting within international NGOs. Experience working in fragile, conflict-affected, or complex operating environments. Strong understanding of the geopolitical, regulatory, and socio-economic contexts across Africa. Experience supporting finance transformation, organisational change, or continuous improvement initiatives. Experience working with local implementing partners and sub-grantees. Why Join Islamic Relief? This role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact across multiple countries by strengthening financial performance, governance, accountability, and sustainability throughout one of the world's leading humanitarian organisations. If you are a strategic finance leader who enjoys developing people, improving systems, driving compliance, and enabling operational excellence across international programmes, we would love to hear from you. For more information, please refer to the full Job Description and Person Specification. If you are talented, reliable, service-minded, resilient, and highly motivated, with a strong commitment to Islamic Relief's mission and values of Sincerity, Excellence, Compassion, Social Justice, and Custodianship, please submit your application via our online recruitment portal. PLEASE NOTE: Interviews may be held on an ongoing basis, and we reserve the right to close this vacancy prior to the advertised closing date should a suitable candidate be identified. Pre-Employment Checks Any employment with Islamic Relief will be subject to: Proof of eligibility to live and work within the UK. Satisfactory references. Appropriate screening and safeguarding checks. Please note that we are only able to consider applications from candidates who already have the right to work in the UK. Sponsorship is not available for this position. Our Values and Commitment to Safeguarding Islamic Relief is committed to preventing all forms of abuse, exploitation, harassment, discrimination, and financial misconduct. We expect all employees and volunteers to share this commitment and uphold the highest standards of conduct. All appointments are subject to satisfactory references and safeguarding checks, including participation in the Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme where applicable. Islamic Relief is an equal opportunities employer.

How to Apply: **For further details about the role and application requirements, please refer to the full Job Description and Person Specification and apply via our online recruitment portal using the link below.** [**Regional Finance Controller**](https://islamic-relief.current-vacancies.com/Jobs/Advert/4327242?cid=1858&t=Regional-Finance-Controller)

description:
Job Title: Country Director, Ethiopia Location: Addis Ababa, Ethiopia (Only candidates who are eligible to work legally without work visa sponsorship in Ethiopia will be considered.) Hiring Salary: ETB 508,934 per month (before taxes) Target Start Date: January 2027 Application Closing Date: October 20, 2026 23:59 EAT This job advert is for an existing vacancy. About Right To Play: For more than 25 years, Right To Play has been protecting, educating, and empowering millions of children each year to rise above adversity through the power of play. We offer programs in 10 countries across Africa, Asia, the Middle East and North America, reaching millions of children each year in some of the most difficult places on earth, helping them to connect, learn and thrive. We do this by harnessing play, one of the most fundamental forces in a child's life, to equip children with the critical skills they need to dismantle barriers and embrace opportunities, in learning and in life. This work is supported by our two global offices in Toronto, Canada and London, UK; and seven National Offices in North America and Europe. Right To Play in Ethiopia is working with government, civil society organizations, communities, teachers and parents to increase access to quality education, enhance primary school children's learning and social emotional skills, promote children's access to inclusive, high quality, play-based Early Childhood Care and Education, provide play-based psychosocial support to improve the holistic well-being of children and young people and address the challenges that children face in host, internally displaced and refugee communities. Learn more about our programs in Ethiopia from our website . Benefits Highlights: Connect and collaborate with a global team who are passionate about protecting, educating and empowering children and youth using the power of play! Culture premised on our Culture Code (accept everyone, make things happen, display courage, demonstrate care, and be playful) Paid leave (20 days annual leave and 3 personal days per year) Competitive benefits such as medical insurance for employee and eligible family members, life insurance for employee, transportation allowance, and communications allowance 10% temporary allowance for Ethiopia employees from October to December 2026 and the next salary review is in January 2027 Learning opportunities and 5 learning and development (L&D) days per year Flexible work arrangements More information on what we offer is available on our website . Job Description: Job Title: Country Director (CD) Grade: 11 Reports to: Vice President, Transformation and Impact Location: Ethiopia Direct Reports: Program Manager, Education Specialist, Finance Manager, People and Culture Specialist, MEL Specialist, Logistics Officer Department: Global Program Unit 1.Purpose: Provides overall strategic and programmatic leadership including business development, fundraising, compliance and risk, financial and people management to ensure the success and growth of the country programme. 2.Accountability & Responsibilities: Governance and representation (20%) Identifies and manages organisational risk , including legal and governance matters, and acts as RTP’s legal representative in country. Represents RTP at country level , engaging government, donors, UN agencies, and NGO coordination platforms to build influence, credibility, and strategic partnerships. Fundraising and Communication (20%) Leads country-level fundraising and resource mobilisation , driving proposal development, donor engagement, and diversified funding partnerships. Leads in-country media and external engagement , strengthening RTP’s profile and ensuring alignment with organisational values and objectives. Strategy development and implementation (15%) Sets and leads the strategic direction of the country programme , ensuring alignment with RTP strategy, national priorities, and legal and regulatory requirements. Programmatic oversight, learning and innovation (15%) Oversees the country programme portfolio , ensuring high-quality delivery, measurable impact for children and young people, and timely reporting to donors, government, and HQ. Promotes collaboration and learning , advising partners on play-based and sport-for-development approaches and embedding evidence-informed practice. Champions innovation and continuous improvement , driving excellence in programming and efficiency across internal systems and processes. Operational management (15%) Provides strategic oversight of finance and administration , including budgeting, expenditure control, audits, grant compliance, and strong internal controls. Holds overall accountability for safeguarding, safety, and security , ensuring compliance with RTP policies and national legislation. Staff and workplace management (15%) Ensures effective people management , including recruitment, performance management, learning and development, payroll, and the promotion of a safe and inclusive culture. Leads, mentors, and develops a diverse country team , fostering staff wellbeing, inclusion, and high performance. Promote Safeguarding, foster a safe, respectful, and accountable work environment by modelling appropriate conduct and addressing any behaviour that undermines a healthy workplace. Perform other duties as assigned 3.Scope (geographical and/or functional), Impact and Autonomy: Oversees all aspects of the country office, providing guidance and support to the team, while serving on the Global Leadership Team to ensure quality program delivery, adherence to budgets, and contributing to global initiatives that enhance organizational systems and processes. 4.Leadership and Staff Management: Leads and develops the Country Management Team through coaching, mentoring, and capability-building while championing a safe, inclusive, and high-performing culture. Oversees People & Culture processes to ensure compliance, best practices, and effective performance management, upholding strong DEIA standards, staff safety, and well-being. Demonstrates integrity and resilience, proactively addressing and mitigating legal risks, including seeking legal advice when necessary. 5.Information Requirement for Decision-Making: Makes decisions based on a combination of internal and external information, often requiring an analytic approach to draw conclusions from incomplete information or non-conclusive information. 6.Innovation and Improvements Drives innovation and continuous improvement to deliver high-quality, impactful programs and more efficient internal systems and ways of working. 7. Relationships & Communications: Internal / External: Builds and sustains strategic relationships with key stakeholders, including donors, government officials, UN agencies, academia, media, NGOs, and local partners, while promoting RTP’s identity and relevance to the needs of vulnerable populations, in alignment with the localization strategy. Leads strategic donor, HQ visits, workshops, represents RTP in high-level meetings, conferences, and media to strengthen its profile. 8. Expertise (Certifications / Education, Professional Experience): Extensive experience in leadership roles within a large or medium international development organization, including: strategic planning, leadership and people management, project management and planning, monitoring and evaluation and financial and risk management. Master’s degree in business administration, social sciences, development studies or related discipline. Experience working in or managing programmes in stable and fragile contexts. Proven success with mobilizing new sources of program funding. Understanding of laws, regulations and cultural dynamics local and international. Fluency in spoken and written Amharic and English Significant experience with a child-focused organization is desirable. 9.Core Competences: Collaboration: Highly collaborative with strong interpersonal skills; excels at working in with a multicultural team and builds rapport and trust to develop strong external partnerships. Growth Mindset: Demonstrates commitment to own professional development and encourages their team to develop their potential, creates a learning culture through effective coaching and mentorship. Communication: Communicates complex operational, technical & strategic issues clearly & credibly to diverse audiences, leveraging strong networks to secure donor funding & influence stakeholders. Resilience: Strong organizational skills and the ability to work under pressure: multi-tasking, meeting deadlines, solving problems creatively and embracing challenges with resilience. Professionalism: Models professionalism and RTP’s values, promoting a safe, inclusive workplace and positive impact for children and youth. Management and Interpersonal Skills : Lead and mentor country team with influence, fostering trust, high performance, and shared ownership of outcome. 10.Additional Information: Expected to travel regularly domestically and occasionally internationally and work outside regular hours.

title: RESPONSABLE DU BUREAU DE PLAIDOYER ET DE LIAISON AUPRÈS DE L’UNION AFRICAINE, Oxfam en Afrique
description:
Type de contrat : Contrat à durée déterminée de 2 ans Grade interne : B1, International Rémunération : conforme à la grille salariale d’Oxfam International. Cette offre comprend les avantages sociaux de base ainsi que les prestations globales applicables au personnel recruté à l’international et relocalisé.Nous considérons que les modalités de travail flexibles sont essentielles pour bâtir le Secrétariat de demain. Nous sommes donc disposés à échanger avec vous sur les modalités susceptibles de vous convenir. Le poste Oxfam en Afrique recherche une personne expérimentée, dotée d’un leadership reconnu et d’un forte capacité d’influence, pour diriger son Bureau de plaidoyer et de liaison auprès de l’Union africaine (UA), basé à Addis-Abeba. En tant que membre de l’Équipe de direction de la Plateforme Afrique, vous piloterez l’engagement d’Oxfam auprès de l’Union africaine et de ses institutions. Vous élaborerez et mettrez en œuvre des stratégies de plaidoyer à fort impact afin d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques à l’échelle continentale. Vous représenterez Oxfam au plus haut niveau auprès de l’UA, nouerez des relations stratégiques et contribuerez à positionner Oxfam comme un partenaire crédible et de confiance. Ce poste joue un rôle central dans la réalisation de la mission d’Oxfam en Afrique : il établit un lien entre les espaces d’élaboration des politiques continentales et les réalités nationales, tout en veillant à ce que les actions de plaidoyer soient cohérentes, porteuses d’impact et ancrées dans les réalités vécues par les communautés. Ce poste relève de la Direction Afrique, avec un rattachement matriciel à la Direction Plaidoyer, Campagnes et Engagement (ACE). Profil recherché Nous recherchons une personne reconnue pour son leadership en matière de plaidoyer et d’influence, disposant d’une solide expérience de collaboration avec l’Union africaine ou des institutions multilatérales comparables. Vous avez démontré votre capacité à concevoir et à mettre en œuvre des stratégies d’influence porteuses d’impact, combinant analyse des politiques, plaidoyer, communication médiatique et partenariats afin de favoriser des changements significatifs. Vous excellez dans l’établissement de relations et la négociation, savez évoluer efficacement dans des environnements complexes associant de multiples parties prenantes et êtes en mesure d’exercer une influence au plus haut niveau. Grâce à votre capacité de réflexion stratégique et d’analyse politique, vous savez traduire les processus de l’UA en possibilités concrètes d’influence et d’impact pour les pays et les partenaires. Votre expérience du leadership vous permet de diriger des équipes diversifiées et de travailler au sein d’un réseau mondial, tout en favorisant la collaboration et la redevabilité. Vous avez une connaissance approfondie du contexte sociopolitique africain et adhérez aux approches féministes, décoloniales et portées par les partenaires. La maîtrise professionnelle de l’anglais et du français est indispensable. Pourquoi nous rejoindre Ce poste offre une occasion rare d’influencer les politiques et les pratiques au plus haut niveau continental. À Oxfam, vous façonnerez notre engagement auprès de l’Union africaine, piloterez le plaidoyer sur des enjeux majeurs tels que les inégalités, la pauvreté et la justice, et collaborerez avec des gouvernements, des diplomates et des institutions internationales pour réaliser des changements concrets. Au sein d’une équipe de direction diversifiée et collaborative, vous contribuerez à rapprocher les politiques continentales des réalités des communautés, afin que les décisions prises au plus haut niveau se traduisent par des résultats tangibles pour les populations partout en Afrique. Ce que nous offrons À Oxfam, nous sommes convaincus que chaque aspect de notre travail peut contribuer à un changement positif. Si vous partagez cette conviction et possédez les compétences nécessaires pour relever les défis liés à ce poste, cette fonction vous offrira de grandes possibilités d’épanouissement personnel ainsi que d’excellentes perspectives d’évolution professionnelle. Oxfam s’engage à proposer une rémunération équitable, sur la base d’une semaine de travail de 36 heures À propos de nous Oxfam est un mouvement mondial de personnes qui agissent ensemble pour mettre fin à l’injustice qu’est la pauvreté. Cela signifie que nous nous attaquons aux inégalités qui maintiennent les populations dans la pauvreté. Ensemble, nous sauvons des vies, protégeons les populations et les aidons à reconstruire leur existence. Lorsqu’une catastrophe survient, nous aidons les personnes à bâtir un avenir meilleur, pour elles-mêmes et pour les autres. Nous agissons sur des enjeux tels que les droits fonciers, le changement climatique et les discriminations à l’égard des femmes. Et nous ne nous arrêterons pas tant que chaque personne sur la planète ne pourra pas vivre à l’abri de la pauvreté. Nous sommes une confédération internationale composée de 22 organisations affiliées et du Secrétariat d’Oxfam International. Avec nos partenaires et les communautés locales, nous menons des actions humanitaires, des programmes de développement et des campagnes dans plus de 76 pays. Oxfam en Afrique (OiA) est une plateforme continentale qui assure la coordination des bureaux pays d’Oxfam en Afrique et collabore avec des organisations de la société civile, des universitaires, des gouvernements et le secteur privé afin de contribuer à une Afrique plus égalitaire, en remettant en cause les structures de pouvoir qui perpétuent les inégalités et les injustices. À cette fin, Oxfam en Afrique apporte un leadership intellectuel dynamique et offre un espace de collaboration à ses partenaires. Oxfam en Afrique joue un rôle moteur dans l’appui aux communautés locales et le renforcement de leur pouvoir d’agir, la promotion de l’égalité de genre, le plaidoyer en faveur de changements de politiques publiques et le renforcement des capacités des organisations locales de la société civile. L’ensemble de notre travail est guidé par nos valeurs fondamentales : Autonomisation, Redevabilité, Inclusion, Courage, Solidarité et Égalité. Notre engagement en matière de safeguarding (Protection contre le harcèlement, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels) Oxfam s’engage à prévenir toute forme de comportement inapproprié au travail, notamment le harcèlement sexuel, l’exploitation et les abus sexuels, les manquements à l’intégrité et les irrégularités financières, ainsi qu’à promouvoir le bien-être des enfants, des jeunes et des adultes. Oxfam attend de l’ensemble de son personnel et de ses volontaires qu’ils partagent cet engagement et respectent notre Code de conduite. Nous accordons une importance primordiale au recrutement de personnes qui partagent nos valeurs et les mettent en pratique. Remarque : Toute offre d’emploi sera subordonnée à la réception de références satisfaisantes et pourra faire l’objet de contrôles appropriés, notamment une vérification du casier judiciaire et des contrôles relatifs au financement du terrorisme. Le Secrétariat d’Oxfam International participe également au Mécanisme interorganisations de divulgation des inconduites (Inter-Agency Misconduct Disclosure Scheme). Conformément à ce dispositif, si une personne candidate a précédemment travaillé pour une autre organisation membre, nous solliciterons auprès de cette organisation des informations concernant toute constatation d’exploitation sexuelle, d’abus sexuels et/ou de harcèlement sexuel survenue pendant son emploi, ainsi que tout incident qui faisait encore l’objet d’une enquête au moment de son départ. En soumettant sa candidature, la personne candidate confirme avoir pris connaissance de cette procédure de recrutement.

How to Apply: **Comment postuler** Si vous souhaitez influencer les politiques continentales et renforcer l’engagement auprès de l’Union africaine afin de favoriser des changements durables en Afrique, nous vous invitons à postuler. Veuillez soumettre un CV à jour et une lettre de motivation via ce lien [https://oxfam.current-vacancies.com/Jobs/Advert/4325897?cid=3360](https://oxfam.current-vacancies.com/Jobs/Advert/4325897?cid=3360) , en démontrant clairement en quoi votre profil répond aux critères essentiels définis dans la fiche de poste de Responsable du Bureau de plaidoyer et de liaison auprès de l’Union africaine. Integrate field observations and stakeholder feedback with secondary data to strengthen expansion assessments and recommendations. description:
The Physiotherapist is responsible for the treatment, counselling, preventative care and rehabilitation of the motor function and physical wellness of the patients. is responsible for assessing, planning, implementing, and evaluating individualized rehabilitation programs for patients with limb loss and other mobility impairments. Working within a multidisciplinary team, the Physiotherapist facilitates functional recovery, promotes independence, optimizes prosthetic use, and improves patients’ quality of life through evidence-based rehabilitation practices The Physiotherapist tasks and responsibilities include, but are not limited to, the following points: Undertake a comprehensive and accurate assessment of patients in a variety of settings; Identify, plan and manage physiotherapy interventions and rehabilitation plans Provide physio treatments to achieve identified outcomes and monitor patients’ conditions, both for in-patients and out-patients, if needed; Perform all the tasks related to the physio competence framework; Establish, maintain and conclude therapeutic interpersonal relationships with patients and their relatives, based on respect, dignity and care; Conduct comprehensive physical assessments of patients with upper and lower limb amputations, including musculoskeletal, neurological, cardiovascular, balance, gait, and functional evaluations. Provide pre-prosthetic rehabilitation, including: residual limb care and shaping, edema management, scar management, pain management (including phantom limb pain where appropriate), range of motion and strengthening exercises, contracture prevention Cardiovascular conditioning Deliver prosthetic rehabilitation, including: prosthetic gait training, balance and coordination training, functional mobility training Stair negotiation and community ambulation Transfers and activities of daily living (ADL) training Fall prevention strategies Monitor patient progress and modify treatment plans according to clinical outcomes. Encourage patients to have a positive attitude towards physiotherapy by motivating them; Organizing daily group activities, if possible, for patients; Promote an environment that enables patient’s safety and health implementing all necessary actions such as infection control practices, bed sores prevention practices and maintaining high level of hygiene also ensuring physio material are properly cleaned; Ensure that the equipment is functional and well maintained and stored; Ensure documentation/record is accurate and physio chart is properly filled, maintaining confidentially of information; Compiling and submitting periodic reports, if requested, following EMERGENCY guidelines; Be compliant with EMERGENCY guidelines for the treatment of patients; Work closely with prosthetists/orthotists during prosthetic prescription, fitting, alignment, and follow-up. Provide clinical feedback regarding prosthetic fit, function, comfort, and patient performance. Participate in training programs or activities, meeting timelines and deliverables, if requested by EMERGENCY; Train new staff, if needed. Job requirements: Degree in the Physio field; (Bachelor’s Degree in Physiotherapy from a recognized institution). Postgraduate training in rehabilitation, prosthetics, amputee rehabilitation, or neurorehabilitation Experience working in prosthetic and orthotic services. Good problem solving, time management and technical skills and willingness to learn new procedures and techniques; Good communication, interpersonal skills and high level of empathy, patience and ability to handle emotional and pressure situations; Basic Computer Skills, including Microsoft Office Program; Good level of English, written and spoken.

title: Ethiopia Driver (Fixed-Term)
description:
About One Acre Fund Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africa's farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions. To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post. In Ethiopia, we engage farmers in agroforestry and community-based seed multiplication to increase farmers’ incomes and make farming systems more resilient. Engaging with local actors at every step but bringing innovative ideas from outside, we are making rural farming more market-friendly and environmentally sustainable. The farmers we work with in Ethiopia have planted more than 30 million trees, produced over 1500 metric tonnes of improved teff seed, and improved the futures of nearly 200,000 community members. Our permanent team numbers over 180 with nearly 1,000 rural seasonal staff supporting them. Our country headquarters are in Addis Ababa and we have a large program office in Bahir Dar, plus several smaller field offices. About the Role Seeking a skilled, careful driver with 3+ years of experience to drive staff and materials for an international agriculture NGO. Remain alert to potential security risks and follow safety procedures during all trips. Maintain a valid driver’s license and inform your supervisor of any changes or violations. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. title: Economic Programming and Private Business Partnerships Advisor
description:

Today, PIN stands as one of the largest organizations of its kind in Central and Eastern Europe, supporting vulnerable communities in Asia, Africa, the Middle East, and Eastern Europe. PIN empowers civil society, advocates for human rights, and promotes social inclusion both at home and abroad. PIN is present in Ethiopia since 2003, works in partnership with communities, local organisations and public institutions to support sustainable development and improve people’s well-being across the country. Through integrated programming, PIN combines immediate assistance with longer-term, systems-oriented approaches aimed at strengthening resilience, expanding access to essential services and economic opportunities, and enabling locally led solutions. description:
Who We Are

Girl Effect is an international non-profit organization dedicated to addressing challenges faced by adolescent girls and youth in Ethiopia. Operating in the country since 2013, the organization leverages Social and Behavior Change (SBC) strategies, combining media and on-the-ground interventions to tackle various societal issues and empower young people. Girl Effect Ethiopia created the youth brand Yegna in 2014 and, since then, has reached over 10 million people through multiple products, outreach programs, girl networks, and research pieces done all for the betterment of adolescent lives.

We create safe spaces for girls, sharing facts and answering questions about health, nutrition, education, relationships, etc. And we use innovative technology so we can reach girls at scale. We arm girls with the skills to negotiate and redefine what they are told is possible, so every girl can choose to be in control of her body, her health, her learning and livelihood.

When a girl unlocks her power to make different choices that change her life, it inspires others to do so too. She starts a ripple effect that impacts her family, community, and country. 

That’s the Girl Effect.

Background

Yegna Gize, meaning “Our Time” in Amharic, is a Girl Effect Ethiopia programme that builds on the Yegna brand and its experience of using media, storytelling, role modelling, and community engagement to influence positive social and behavioural change among young people. Yegna Gize focuses specifically on youth economic empowerment, with an emphasis on improving young peoples aspirations, mindsets, skills, access to opportunities, and pathways towards employment and entrepreneurship.

Over the programme period, Yegna Gize seeks to contribute to improved economic opportunities and livelihood outcomes for young people in Ethiopia by addressing barriers related to employment, entrepreneurship, skills development, social norms, and mindsets. The programme works with young people, schools, communities, government institutions, civil society organisations (CSOs), private-sector actors, role models, and other relevant stakeholders to create an enabling environment for youth to pursue viable economic pathways.

The programme is implemented across six regions of Ethiopia: Tigray, Oromia, Amhara, Central Ethiopia, Sidama, and South Ethiopia. Through a combination of youth-centred interventions, partnerships, capacity strengthening, communication and social and behavioural change approaches, Yegna Gize aims to strengthen young peoples knowledge, skills, confidence, aspirations, networks, and access to employment and entrepreneurship opportunities.

Key areas of Yegna Gize programming include:

  • Youth employment and transition to work: Supporting young people to access internships, work-based learning, employment opportunities, and other pathways into the labour market.
  • Entrepreneurship and enterprise development: Strengthening entrepreneurial knowledge, business skills, growth mindsets, and access to support for young people interested in starting or growing businesses.
  • Skills and mindset development: Building practical, transferable, entrepreneurial, and employability skills, alongside confidence, aspirations, resilience, and positive attitudes towards work and entrepreneurship.
  • Peer-to-peer and youth support mechanisms: Establishing and strengthening youth groups and peer-support approaches that enable young people to learn from and support one another.
  • Role modelling and mentorship: Connecting young people with role models, mentors, entrepreneurs, and other influential individuals who can provide inspiration, guidance, and practical exposure to different livelihood pathways.
  • School-based engagement: Working with schools, teachers, students, and relevant stakeholders to promote entrepreneurship, creativity, growth mindset, career aspirations, and awareness of economic opportunities.
  • Youth-centred media and social and behavioural change communication (SBC): Using Yegnas established multimedia and storytelling platforms to challenge limiting norms, promote positive attitudes towards work and entrepreneurship, and increase young peoples awareness and uptake of available opportunities.
  • Partnerships and systems strengthening: Working with regional and local government structures, CSOs, private-sector actors, educational institutions, and other stakeholders to strengthen the ecosystem supporting youth economic empowerment.

Girl Effect works with local partners to contextualise and implement interventions according to regional realities and the needs of young people. The programme therefore combines national-level approaches with locally relevant implementation, allowing interventions to respond to the different economic, social, cultural, and institutional contexts across the six regions.

Yegna Gize Programme Impact Study

As the programme progresses, Girl Effect Ethiopia intends to commission an independent Impact Study of Yegna Gize to assess the extent to which the programme has contributed to changes in young peoples knowledge, skills, attitudes, aspirations, behaviours, access to opportunities, and economic outcomes.

The study is expected to generate credible evidence on the effectiveness, relevance, and contribution of Yegna Gize interventions and to identify which approaches are working, for whom, under what conditions, and why. The findings will inform programme learning, adaptation, accountability to stakeholders and donors, and future programming and scale-up decisions.

The selected agency will therefore be expected to develop and implement a rigorous and contextually appropriate study methodology that captures both quantitative and qualitative evidence, where appropriate, and considers the diversity of young people, intervention types, implementation approaches, and regional contexts within Yegna Gize. The study should generate actionable evidence and recommendations that can strengthen the programmes contribution to sustainable youth economic empowerment in Ethiopia.

Girl Effect is looking to engage a qualified agency to recruit, train, and deploy experienced data collectors across the specified geographic scope, and to manage the full data collection cycle, from fieldwork through to data analysis and submission in line with Girl Effect Ethiopias tools, sample design, and quality standards.

2.3 Training

The agency will organize and deliver training for all data collectors before each deployment, covering:

  • Use of Girl Effect Ethiopias data collection tools and mobile data collection platform.
  • The sample design and how it translates into fieldwork assignments.

  • Logistics, reporting lines, and escalation procedures for field issues.

Girl Effect Ethiopia will provide technical content on the tools and safeguarding standards; the agency is responsible for organizing, scheduling, and delivering the training itself, and for confirming collector competency before deployment (e.g., through a short practical assessment or pilot/pre-test).

description:
About One Acre Fund

Founded in 2006, One Acre Fund equips 5.5 million smallholder farmers to make their farms more productive. Across nine countries that together are home to two-thirds of Africas farmers, we provide high-quality farm supplies, tree seedlings, accessible credit, modern agronomic training, and a wide range of other agricultural services. On average, this model enables any farmer to increase their income and assets on supported land by more than 35 percent, while permanently improving their resilience. This is all made possible by our team of 9,000+ full-time staff, drawn from diverse backgrounds and professions.

To learn more, please see our Why Work Here blog post.

One Acre Fund has been working with farmers in the Amhara region of Ethiopia since 2014, with a specific focus on trees since 2018. The Ethiopia program has now expanded into the South Region of Ethiopia in 2024. Our aim with the tree program is to provide not only short-term income opportunities but also long-term benefits, such as soil health improvements and erosion control, so that farmers build resilience over time.

About the Role

The Innovations & Growth Lead will be an essential part of our leadership team in one of One Acre Funds fastest-growing country programs and report directly to the Country Director. 

As an Innovations & Growth Lead, you will sit at the intersection of high-level strategy and "last-mile" delivery, shaping the strategy to plant 100 million trees and generate over $100M additional impact for 440,000 Ethiopian farmers by 2030. You will also pioneer the revenue models that will make our impact self-sustaining.

You will lead a high-performing team of innovators and M&E specialists to turn a 5-year vision into a rigorous Learning Agenda”: designing the field trials, mastering the data, and proving what works before we scale it to 440,000 households. You will ensure that every piece of data collected in the field informs our highest-level strategic decisions. If you are obsessed with evidence-based growth and love solving complex operational puzzles in the field, this is for you!.

Success is measured by your ability to reach OAF Ethiopia’s 2030 objectives. You will:

  • Support our network of 1,000+ nursery managers by improving their production and finding new ways to generate income.
  • Engineer innovative, scalable solutions to maximize income for every farmer reached, unlocking opportunities for youth and women.
  • Secure our seed supply through large-scale adoption of the best varieties and partnerships like the Jimma Research Centre.
  • Define the next frontier and move beyond existing programs to identify "whats next." You will lead the feasibility studies to transition OAF Ethiopia from a traditional NGO model to a revenue-generating organization. You will investigate the regulatory landscape and operational requirements, and research and test the most impactful agricultural practices, products, and services for our farmers.

In a single week, you could present our Learning Agenda to our Steerco, deciding which new programs (like carbon credits or market access) are ready for a pilot and which arent yet viable. You would then work with the Tree innovation team to turn raw avocado trial data into a "Go/No-Go" recommendation for national expansion, before travelling to a remote nursery to troubleshoot a pilot in person, interviewing nursery managers to identify why avocado grafting success rates are lagging, and pivoting the training approach on the spot.

Responsibilities

  • Translate our strategy into action: Lead multi-year impact strategies and translate them into specific field interventions across the organization.
  • Drive the "Learning Agenda": Define annual critical questions. You will decide which new services or products enter our pipeline based on scale and ROI, then set SMART objectives. For example, explore the possibility of adding high-value trees.
  • End-to-End Trial Management:  Design multi-year impact models, oversee the full lifecycle of field trials, empower and coach the impact team to research and implement impactful activities, from hypothesis and budgeting to operational workflows and staff training to translating it into actionable recommendations.
  • Evidence-Based Decision Making: Partner with our Monitoring & Evaluation teams to analyze trial data and drive "Go/No-Go" recommendations for the Country Director. 
  • Champion the professional evolution of your direct reports, providing the coaching and clarity needed to turn high-level organizational vision into rigorous, field-level results.

Career Growth and Development

We have a strong culture of constant learning, and we invest in developing our people. You’ll have weekly check-ins with your manager, access to mentorship and training programs, and regular feedback on your performance. We hold career reviews every six months and set aside time to discuss your aspirations and career goals. You’ll have the opportunity to shape a growing organization and build a rewarding long-term career.

Qualifications

Across all roles, these are the general qualifications we look for. For this role specifically, you will have:

  • A proven track record with a minimum of 7 years of experience in managing complex projects or operations, or social enterprise programs in emerging markets, e.g., in agricultural innovation, extension, research & development, marketing, product development, consulting or MEL in agriculture, public health, or education (including 3+ years in one of our countries of operation).
  • Experience identifying strategic gaps and designing "Learning Agendas" - knowing exactly which questions we need to answer through field trials before committing to a national-scale rollout.
  • Field-First Mindset: Significant experience living and working in rural or "last-mile" settings, with a deep understanding of the associated operational challenges.
  • Experimental Design & "Piloting" Mindset: Proven ability to design and execute field trials or pilot programs. You understand how to set up a "test vs. control" environment to see if a new intervention actually drives impact, you understand KPIs and success metrics and you have the judgment to adjust as needed when challenges come.
  • Evaluation Frameworks: Analyze qualitative/quantitative field data, and turn raw results into a "Go/No-Go" recommendation for leadership. A plus if experience working with Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) teams to design surveys.
  • Experience managing large teams (5-10+ team members) and delivering projects successfully.
  • English required, Amharic preferred. 

Preferred Start Date

As soon as possible

Job Location

On-site in Addis Ababa or Bahir Dar, Ethiopia, with regular visits to our field areas of operations (around 35% of the time).

Benefits

Health insurance, housing, and comprehensive benefits

Eligibility

One Acre Fund can support a work permit for this role. However, nationals of (or those with an extensive professional background and work history in) our countries of operation are preferred.

 

Please note that we hire on a rolling basis which means that applications are reviewed and processed on a continuous basis until a hire is made.

One Acre Fund never asks candidates to pay any money or pay for tests at any stage of the interview process. Official One Acre Fund emails will always arrive from an @oneacrefund.org address. Please report any suspicious communication here (globalhotline@oneacrefund.org), but do not send applications or application materials to this email address.
